We talk a lot here about homemade guns, gun ideas, and caliber options for these, but I never see .45lc discussed in those topics. Why not? I think .45lc would make a great option for homemade firearms.

The pressure on these is very low! Lower than a .380acp, standard max pressure 21,000 kPa. For the .45lc standard max pressure is 14,000 kPa. That's only 2/3 of the .380.

Many of the open-bolt DIY SMG designs I see recommend using .380 acp for it's low pressure, but why not pick something with an even lower pressure that puts bigger holes in shit? Especially if those bigger holes are made by something going under the speed of sound? Better suppression.

A lower pressure also implies that I can use a lighter bolt, or if using a heavier bolt, can more easily control my rate of fire. If we understand peak pressure to be the most important aspect of firearm locking and cycling, we can assume that this will be a 'safer' round to experiment with than others like 9mm or 9kurz.

The fact that a .45lc is a rimmed cartridge shouldn't hurt this effort either. Plenty of pistols use the rimmed .22lr and function fine.

Size. Front to rear, the .45lc I have in front of me is ~4cm. My 'glock' frame pistol hase a grip that is between 6cm and 5cm variable from front to back. No problem making a steel, sheet metal grip that houses a .45lc mag that is also comfotable. Plenty of space if you consider you probably won't be adding more than 6mm width overall.
